title: Manappuram Finance Ltd - 531213 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Manappuram Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 45% QoQ to INR585 crore, with consolidated AUM up 9% QoQ to INR69,635 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~12% QoQ, ~98% YoY; vs 80% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated PAT (before OCI and minority interest)
financial_highlights.change: up 45% QoQ (management also cited 44.5%), up 47% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR7,188 crore (incl. INR2,344 crore gold loan AUM)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR13 crore in Q4 FY26; loss of INR269 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Up about 10 bps in Q1 FY27 (about 20 bps per analyst question)

financial_highlights.change: vs 57.3% in March 2026; management attributed rise mainly to gold price fall

segments.name: Gold loans (standalone)
segments.commentary: AUM INR54,655 crore, 90% of standalone AUM (87% in Q4 FY26); 26.5 lakh outstanding customers after adding about 3.2 lakh in Q1; about 86% of gold loan book is online.

segments.name: Asirvad Microfinance
segments.commentary: AUM INR7,188 crore, up 5.8% QoQ; PAT INR21 crore; net NPA 1.4%; CRAR 31%. Management aims to cap microfinance at 8%-10% of consolidated AUM.

segments.name: Vehicle finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,562 crore, down 14.3% QoQ and 43% YoY; GNPA 13.3% vs 10.4% in Q4. Management has temporarily stopped vehicle lending and is focused on collections.

segments.name: MSME and allied
segments.commentary: Loans INR3,303 crore with disbursement of INR191 crore in the quarter; GNPA 5.9% vs 7.1% in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Home loans (Manappuram Home Finance)
segments.commentary: Book INR1,847 crore, flat QoQ and down about 3% YoY. Company has begun lending in Manappuram Home Finance, with gold loans planned under co-lending and qualifying-asset limits.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in the RBI LTV framework implementation, and what income-generating loan products were launched?
qa_highlights.answer: Income-generating gold loans (monthly EMI and quarterly products) launched from April 1 with ticket bands up to INR2.5 lakh, INR2.5-5 lakh and above INR5 lakh; interest rate 14%-16%; internal LTV cap 85%, versus overall average LTV of about 64%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 60 bps gold loan yield improvement and will it hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was driven by pricing actions taken after over-correction in Q4, not by mix shift; expects yield to stay in a band around 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LTV rise from 57% to 65.6% a numerator or denominator change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a denominator effect from the gold price drop; the numerator now includes some interest under the new RBI definition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 gold loan growth guidance and steady-state yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected gold loan growth of about 25%-30% for FY27; yield around 18% with a plus or minus 25 bps range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Asirvad provision increase QoQ and cost of borrowing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 included one-off releases of about INR9 crore; Q1 reflects a normalised provision cycle. Management sees room to renegotiate borrowing costs given secured gold share above 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term microfinance and strategic priority plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Microfinance to be capped at 8%-10% of consolidated AUM with gold at 75%-80% of AUM; vehicle lending paused, with a possible restart in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Gold loan AUM growth for FY27 expected around 25%-30% (management cited about 30% in one answer), with seasonality across quarters; Q1 gold loan growth was about 12% QoQ.
Gold loan yield expected around 18%, with a possible move of plus or minus 25 bps; pricing is expected to stay in a broad band around 18%.
Plan to open around 500 branches in FY27 across Manappuram and Asirvad gold loan branches, enabled by removal of RBI prior approval; management expects a good improvement in branch openings from Q2.
Target to keep gold loans at 75%-80% of consolidated AUM; microfinance to be capped at 8%-10% of consolidated AUM.
Medium-term targets: ROA of around 3.5%-4% and ROE of 15%-18%, with ROE around 18% in three years.
Incremental cost of funds expected around 8.8%-9%; management said it is hard to predict where the average cost of funds will settle.
Microfinance disbursement growth expected at about INR400-500 crore per quarter; no vehicle loan disbursements in FY27, with a possible review in FY28.
Asirvad is negotiating with lenders for lower borrowing costs given over 30% of its book is now secured gold loans.
capex_capacity: Plan to open around 500 gold loan branches in the current year after RBI removed prior-approval requirement; 500 target covers Manappuram and Asirvad branches.
Branch mix: around 60% in South and Central India (five South states plus Maharashtra), about 25% in eastern states (Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha and others), balance in rest of India.
Only about 10 branches were added in Q1 FY27 per analyst reading of the presentation; management said pace will be low initially and pick up.
Income-generating loans launched from April 1, 2026 with EMI and monthly-interest options; staff trained for about six months before rollout.
Management said the company has hired staff for cash-flow-based products.
demand_pricing: Gold loan tonnage and customer growth reportedly held up in Q1 despite seasonal slowness and continued into July and August, per management.
Gold price fell about 8.5% (INR14,161 at March-end to INR12,954 at June-30), pushing average LTV up to 65.6%; management said LTV normally runs 64%-67%.
Management said its gold loan pricing is at the lowest range in the NBFC industry and it must move with the market amid strong competition.
Ticket-size mix of gold loans: up to INR1 lakh 21%, INR1-3 lakh 30%, above INR3 lakh 49%.
Customer mix is shifting toward business and MSME borrowers; attrition at branches is about 2%-2.5% per month.
risks_watch: Gold price volatility drives LTV (65.6% in Q1, rising from 57.3%) and collateral cover; management said the average LTV could fall further after the last week's price rise.
Competition in gold loans may force pricing or margin pressure; management said it will balance margin against growth.
Rising funding costs: standalone borrowing cost up about 10 bps; marginal cost seen at 8.8%-9% with MIFOR at all-time highs.
Vehicle finance GNPA at 13.3% and MSME GNPA at 5.9%; collections focus is key.
Execution risk on 500 branch openings, with only about 10 added in Q1; income-generating loan book is new and small.
CEO transition: Ashish Singh to join as MD and CEO by January 1, 2027.
key_quotes: Consolidated AUM for Q1 '27 was at INR69,635 crores, up by 9% QOQ and up by 57% year -on-year.
We are targeting an ROA of around 3.5% to 4%, and targeting an ROE of 15% to 18%, which is the ROE target.
We want to contain microfinance at below 10% at a consolidated level.
Our attrition level remained around 2% to 2.5% per month.
summary.management_tone: Confident on gold loan growth, yield stabilisation and branch expansion, with management stating the Q1 numbers and pricing actions are delivering. Cautious and sometimes evasive on funding cost trajectory, incremental yield on new income-generating products, and the portfolio-level breakdown, which management deferred to later sharing.
